doc.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000

chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and the Oscar Peterson Trio
title: The Oscar Peterson Trio and arranged music
summary: Brown describes the trio as a peak in which his JATP experience came out, and why the group was so arranged after years of jamming.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: The stint with Oscar. At that time in your career, musically, was that as about a high peak as you’d been to? I’m not sure I asked that question very well, but he must have challenged you and you challenged him and Herb and back and forth.

Yeah. It was a good era for all of us because this, after all of us being with Jazz at the Philharmonic and now we wind up with that group, there’s a lot of stuff that you have accrued over those years of playing with all those giants. And now all of this stuff can come out, and it comes out in various forms.
The music was quite arranged in a lot of places.

Yes. As a matter of fact I think that’s part of — well people ask me, they said how come you have such an arranged group? I mean everything is laid out and picture perfect you know. I said probably because I jammed for twenty-five years every night. And you get tired of that too.

I think it’s refreshing, especially these days, to hear a group that’s played together and rehearsed together. I mean jamming is fine too, but sometimes it’s nice, I love the arranged part of jazz too.

Oh yeah. Because you’ve got to remember the arrangement part of jazz is only in certain spots. There’s a lot of freedom for guys to blow, everybody has got a lot of free space there. And I mean if you hear somebody play the same tune five nights in a row, the blowing’s going to be different. The parts are the same, but the blowing’s different. And if you get a jam session like one of these jam sessions here, if you’ve got the same group to play together for three weeks, five or six nights a week, they would start sounding like a band too. It would just happen like that.
